items.title: Building Serverless Python Apps Using AWS Chalice
items.description: Build and deploy a serverless Python app with AWS Chalice, a microframework that ships your code to AWS Lambda and scales it for you.
items.summary: Shipping a web application usually involves having your code up and running on single or multiple servers. In this model, you end up setting up processes for monitoring, provisioning, and scaling your servers up or down.

items.title: Sets in Python
items.description: Learn to work effectively with Python sets: define set objects, explore the supported operations, and know when sets fit your code.
items.summary: Python provides a built-in set data type. It differs from other built-in data types in that it’s an unordered collection of unique elements.

items.title: Sending Emails With Python
items.description: Learn how to send emails with Python using SMTP, attach files, format HTML messages, and personalize bulk emails for your contact list.
items.summary: You probably found this tutorial because you want to send emails with Python to automate confirmation messages, password resets, or scheduled notifications. Python’s standard library covers the whole pipeline, from making a server connection to building the message and sending it to one or many recipients.

items.title: Python Performance Optimization: A Practical Guide
items.description: Learn practical Python performance optimization techniques, from confirming a bottleneck with timeit to picking the fix that makes your program faster.
items.summary: Python performance optimization is the practice of making your code run faster. You find the bottleneck first, then fix only what’s slow, starting with algorithms and data structures before reaching for concurrency or C extensions.

items.title: Python itertools By Example
items.description: Combine Python's itertools functions into memory-efficient pipelines as you deal cards, analyze stock data, and pick relay teams.
items.summary: Python’s itertools module is one of the hidden gems of the standard library. Knowing the definitions of its functions isn’t enough, though.

items.title: Python itertools By Example
items.description: Master Python's itertools module by building practical examples with batched(), pairwise(), groupby(), and more, and learn to think iteratively.
items.summary: It has been called a “gem” and “pretty much the coolest thing ever,” and if you haven’t heard of it, then you’re missing out on one of the greatest corners of the Python standard library : itertools . Knowing the definitions of its functions isn’t enough, though.

items.title: Pygame: A Primer on Game Programming in Python
items.description: Learn how Pygame lets you build games and rich multimedia programs in Python: draw to the screen, detect collisions, and handle input.
items.summary: When I started learning computer programming late in the last millennium, it was driven by my desire to write computer games. I tried to figure out how to write games in every language and on every platform I learned, including Python.

items.title: Operators and Expressions in Python
items.description: Python operators are the symbols and keywords that build expressions. Learn how to combine them with objects to compute real results.
items.summary: Python operators enable you to perform computations by combining objects and operators into expressions. Understanding Python operators is essential for manipulating data effectively.

items.title: Python Plotting With Matplotlib (Guide)
items.description: This article is a beginner-to-intermediate-level walkthrough on Python and matplotlib that mixes theory with example.
items.summary: A picture is worth a thousand words, and with Python’s matplotlib library, it fortunately takes far less than a thousand words of code to create a production-quality graphic. However, matplotlib is also a massive library, and getting a plot to look just right is often achieved through trial and error.

items.title: Speed Up Your Python Program With Concurrency
items.description: Explore Python concurrency with threading, asyncio, and multiprocessing, and learn which model speeds up your I/O-bound or CPU-bound programs.
items.summary: Concurrency refers to the ability of a program to manage multiple tasks at once, improving performance and responsiveness. It encompasses different models like threading, asynchronous tasks, and multiprocessing, each offering unique benefits and trade-offs.

items.title: Python and REST APIs: Interacting With Web Services
items.description: Learn to consume web services with the requests library, then explore the tools for building a Python REST API of your own.
items.summary: There’s an amazing amount of data available on the Web. Many web services , like YouTube and GitHub, make their data accessible to third-party applications through an application programming interface (API) .

items.title: Supply Chain Security for the Age of AI-Speed Exploits
items.description: Learn Python supply chain security as AI speeds up attacks: what the LiteLLM backdoor teaches, how to check your setup, and habits that last.
items.summary: Python supply chain security means protecting everything your project pulls in and runs, from PyPI packages to CI workflows and publishing credentials, so that a tampered release or stolen token can’t turn your own tools against you. AI-assisted analysis makes it cheaper to turn a bug fix into a working exploit, so attacks now arrive within hours of a fix, and sometimes before it.

items.title: Reading and Writing CSV Files in Python
items.description: Learn how Python handles CSV files: read, write, and parse them with the built-in csv library, and see how pandas does the same job.
items.summary: Let’s face it: you need to get information into and out of your programs through more than just the keyboard and console . Exchanging information through text files is a common way to share info between programs.

items.title: Emacs: The Best Python Editor?
items.description: Install and configure Emacs for Python development, then write, run, test, and debug your Python code without leaving the editor.
items.summary: Finding the right code editor for Python development can be tricky. Many developers explore numerous editors as they grow and learn.

items.title: Python Program Lexical Structure
items.description: Dig into the Python program structure: the syntactic elements that make up statements, and how statements group into larger blocks.
items.summary: You have now covered Python variables , operators, and data types in depth, and you’ve seen quite a bit of example code. Up to now, the code has consisted of short individual statements, simply assigning objects to variables or displaying values.

items.title: How to Automate Your Workflow With Claude Code Hooks
items.description: Learn how to use Claude Code hooks that auto-format your Python code after every edit, enforce your chosen tools, and ping you when a task finishes.
items.summary: When you pair with Claude Code, some steps shouldn’t be left to chance, and Claude Code hooks are how you lock them in. You want a heads-up when it finishes a long task, a guarantee that it sticks to your project’s approved tools, and a promise that every edit is formatted to your code standards, without repeating yourself each time.

items.title: How to Round Numbers in Python
items.description: Learn how Python's round() works, why it rounds 2.5 to 2, and how you can manage rounding errors with decimal, NumPy, and pandas.
items.summary: Rounding numbers in Python is an essential task, especially when dealing with data precision. Python’s built-in round() function uses the rounding half to even strategy, which rounds numbers like 2.5 to 2 and 3.5 to 4 .

items.title: Asynchronous Tasks With Django and Celery
items.description: Integrate Django and Celery with Redis as a message broker, and move slow work like sending email out of the request cycle.
items.summary: Celery is a distributed task queue that processes tasks asynchronously, so slow work doesn’t hold up your web app’s response. When you integrate Celery with your Django application, you can offload time-consuming tasks and keep your users from waiting.

items.title: Digging Deeper Into Django Migrations
items.description: Go beyond the basics of Django migrations: how they work under the hood, what the Django migrations table tracks, and what's inside migration files.
items.summary: You already understand the purpose of Django migrations and you’re familiar with fundamental usage patterns like creating and applying migrations. In this tutorial, you’ll dig deeper into the migration system and take a peek at some of its underlying mechanics, from the Django migrations table to the migration files themselves.

items.title: Python's Mutable vs Immutable Types: What's the Difference?
items.description: Learn how Python mutable and immutable data types work internally and how you can use mutability or immutability to power your code.
items.summary: Python’s mutable objects, such as lists and dictionaries, allow you to change their value or data directly without affecting their identity. In contrast, immutable objects, like tuples and strings, don’t allow in-place modifications.

items.title: Django Migrations: A Primer
items.description: Get comfortable with Django migrations: create database tables without writing SQL, and keep your database in step as your models change.
items.summary: Since version 1.7, Django has come with built-in support for database migrations. In Django , database migrations usually go hand in hand with models: whenever you code up a new model, you also generate a migration to create the necessary table in the database.

items.title: The Best IDEs and Code Editors for Python (Guide)
items.description: Compare the best Python IDEs and code editors side by side, with free picks for beginners and pro tools for data science and AI-assisted coding.
items.summary: Choosing the best IDE or code editor for Python means weighing your skill level, project type, and workflow in a landscape that has changed dramatically in recent years. AI-first editors have arrived, and well-established tools have added AI integrations.

items.title: Python's Instance, Class, and Static Methods Demystified
items.description: Compare instance methods vs class methods vs static methods in Python, and learn when each one earns its place in your code.
items.summary: Instance, class, and static methods each serve a distinct role in Python, and knowing when to use one over another is key to writing clean, maintainable code. Instance methods operate on individual objects using self , while class methods use cls to access class-level data.

items.title: Python Histogram Plotting: NumPy, Matplotlib, pandas & Seaborn
items.description: In this tutorial, you'll be equipped to make production-quality, presentation-ready Python histogram plots with a range of choices and features.
items.summary: In this tutorial, you’ll be equipped to make production-quality, presentation-ready Python histogram plots with a range of choices and features. If you have introductory to intermediate knowledge in Python and statistics , then you can use this article as a one-stop shop for building and plotting histograms in Python using libraries from its scientific stack, including NumPy, Matplotlib, pandas , and Seaborn.

items.title: How to Create a Django Project
items.description: Learn how to create a Django project and app in clear, guided steps. Use it as a reference for any future Django project and tutorial you'll work on.
items.summary: Before you can start building your Django web application , you need to set up your Django project. Use this tutorial as your go-to reference until you’ve built so many projects that the necessary commands become second nature.

items.title: How to Use Claude Code Skills for Better Python Docstrings
items.description: Learn how to use Claude Code skills to write consistent Python docstrings, with style references and a helper script you can reuse in every project.
items.summary: With Claude Code skills, you can turn a docstring convention you keep re-explaining into instructions that Claude follows on its own. After working through this guide, you can write consistent Python docstrings with a reusable Claude Code skill.

items.title: Building an AI Agent With LangGraph and Python
items.description: Learn LangGraph in Python with this hands-on video course and build a stateful AI agent using state graphs, nodes, and conditional edges.
items.summary: LangGraph is a versatile Python framework designed for stateful, cyclic, and multi-actor Large Language Model (LLM) applications. LangGraph builds on its parent library, LangChain, and allows you to build sophisticated workflows that can handle the complexities of real-world LLM applications.

items.title: Quiz: Building an AI Agent With LangGraph and Python
items.description: Test your understanding of LangGraph state graphs, nodes, edges, and tools, and see how well you can follow an AI agent through its workflow.
items.summary: In this quiz, you’ll test your understanding of Building an AI Agent With LangGraph and Python . The course builds an email-processing agent that reads an incoming email, decides which of its tools to call, and pulls structured details out of the message.
